baseline.answer: When the indexed tool results total at or below `options.triggerChars` (and at least one tool result exists), `maskObservations` returns the messages copied unchanged with `applied: false`, `maskedCount: 0`, `charsRemoved: 0`, and `totalObservationChars` set to the measured total. The exact `skippedReason` value is `'below_trigger'`.

optimized.answer: When there is at least one tool result but `totalChars <= options.triggerChars`, `maskObservations` returns early without masking anything: a copy of the original `messages`, `maskedCount: 0`, `charsRemoved: 0`, `applied: false`, and `totalObservationChars` set to the computed `totalChars`. The exact `skippedReason` value is `'below_trigger'`.

baseline.answer: Non-text children (images, binary data) are never masked — they are filtered out of the collapse and preserved as-is, appended after the single text placeholder — because their size isn't the problem and losing them would be silent.

optimized.answer: Non-text children such as images or binary data are preserved as-is: the masked tool result's content becomes the placeholder text followed by all original non-text children (`part.content.filter(child => child.kind !== 'text')`), so only text children collapse into the single placeholder.

baseline.answer: If `maskObservations` throws internally, the `catch` block returns `unchanged('failed')` — the input messages copied unchanged, with `maskedCount: 0`, `charsRemoved: 0`, `totalObservationChars: 0`, and `applied: false`. The exact `skippedReason` value is `'failed'`.

optimized.answer: If `maskObservations` throws internally, the `catch` block returns `unchanged('failed')` — a copy of the original `messages` array with `maskedCount: 0`, `charsRemoved: 0`, `totalObservationChars: 0`, and `applied: false`. The exact `skippedReason` value is `'failed'`.

optimized.answer: `'stale_file'` — when `sha256(content) !== range.fileContentHash`, `rehydrateExact` returns `{ status: 'stale_file', ... }` with a reason noting the file changed after the snapshot was captured.

baseline.answer: `'unavailable'` — when the content includes a NUL byte, `rehydrateExact` returns `{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'The source file is binary.' }`.

optimized.answer: `'unavailable'` — with the reason `'The source file is binary.'`

baseline.answer: It returns a full-document fallback only when retrieval was attempted but admitted no usable evidence — i.e. the retriever reported `sufficiency: 'unusable'` (or, absent that tri-state, `selectedCount` of 0).

optimized.answer: Only when retrieval's three-way sufficiency came back as `unusable` — per `RetrievalOutcome`, that is the only state that justifies attaching a whole file (`incomplete_declared` still has evidence and declares its gap).

baseline.answer: `estimate_after_failure` — the catch block returns that method, keeping `tokens` at the estimate and applying the 5% conservative margin only when testing `withinBudget`.

optimized.answer: `estimate_after_failure` — when `model.countTokens` throws (or returns a non-finite/non-positive value, which is converted into a throw), the catch branch returns `method: 'estimate_after_failure'`, falling back to the estimate with a conservative margin.

baseline.answer: No. `planRepack` only ever drops optional items (lowest `value` first, ties broken by id); mandatory items and the user's own instruction are never dropped. If mandatory evidence alone still exceeds the budget, the plan comes back with `fits: false` and the reason that mandatory evidence alone exceeds the budget — the request fails closed rather than sending a payload missing evidence it declared it needed.

optimized.answer: No. `planRepack` only ever removes items from the `optional` list (lowest `value` first, ties broken by `id`); mandatory items stay in `kept` throughout. If mandatory evidence alone exceeds the budget, the loop runs out of optional candidates and the plan is returned with `fits: false` and the reason that mandatory evidence alone exceeds the budget — the request fails closed rather than sending a payload missing evidence it declared it needed (`engine/authoritativeCount.ts:127-161`).

baseline.answer: It's anchored one epoch behind the current epoch boundary — at `(epoch - 1) * epochTokens` — so the retained window always holds between one and two epochs of history.

optimized.answer: The retained window is anchored one epoch behind the current boundary — at `(epoch - 1) * epochTokens` — so it always holds between one and two epochs of history.
